case.t0_rule: WHO declaration of a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (docs/DAC_PPE_CODING.md §2)
case.response_scale: Belgian federal government (SPF SPSCAE / FOD VVVL purchasing); provincial, regional and municipal acts are context
case.start_rule: First purchase order or contract for PPE for general supply; inquiries, options-only, tenders and single-mission purchases excluded

inclusion_rules.firm_order: First federal purchase order or contract for PPE for general supply
inclusion_rules.binding_act: First legally binding federal act concerning the PPE response
inclusion_rules.dedicated_funding: First funding legally earmarked for PPE
inclusion_rules.delivery: First physical delivery to municipalities; supplier deliveries to the federal stock and deliveries to hospitals are secondary end points
inclusion_rules.institutionalisation: First permanent body created for the hazard

observation_window.reason: First wave; opens 1 Jan so that pre-t0 events can be context (docs/DAC_PPE_CODING.md §5)

case.identification: Paired federal orders of the same good on different dates (FFP2, surgical masks) can test a delay common to the purchasing service (equal lags for orders of different goods placed together) and, per good, decision-limited vs supply-limited delay only if order dates are spread more widely than delivery variation and placed before supply recovered (Proposition 1). Deliveries are to the federal stock, not to municipalities, so paired lags are measured at that secondary end point.
